title: commcompute-conductor-hierarchical-prefetch-kernel-swap
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel runtime: hierarchical comm/compute conductor that overlaps NCCL collectives with kernel execution; adaptive KV-cache prefetching; kernel swap hinting to reduce stall time. Rollout: canary then full. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: TP workloads continue to be dominated by periods where collectives stall local kernel work or where KV-cache misses force synchronous prefetches that block dispatch. On modern multi-GPU hosts these stalls amplify tail latency and hurt sustained throughput for small-to-medium microbatches used by Redwood hosted customers.

This PR implements a 'commcompute conductor' that coordinates three complementary optimizations for tensor-parallel runtimes: (1) hierarchical collective scheduling and NCCL stream affinity to permit asynchronous overlap with compute across heterogeneous link rates; (2) an adaptive KV-cache prefetcher that issues speculative prefetches based on per-request prefix hit probability and observed token arrival patterns; (3) kernel-swap hinting and lightweight state migration so we can opportunistically launch lower-latency kernels while a large allreduce is in-flight.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- New runtime component: src/runtime/tp/commcompute_conductor.cc/h (C++): orchestrates per-layer schedules, establishes per-peer affinity groups and issues NCCL group launches with calibrated concurrency windows. Contains a compact state machine and exposes hooks for the prefetcher and kernel-swap controller.
- NCCL tuning: src/runtime/nccl/pacing_policy.cc and config: adds per-link bandwidth smoothing and backoff heuristics to avoid oversubscription on mixed NVLink/PCIe topologies.
- KV-cache prefetcher: src/runtime/cache/kv_prefetcher.*: lightweight sampling-based predictor using exponential decay on prefix-hit counts; issues async prefetch RPCs to local caching layer and records soft-failure histograms to tune aggressiveness at runtime.
- Kernel swap: src/runtime/launcher/kernel_swap.*: annotate kernels with 'swap_hint' metadata, enable faster microkernel fallback paths when large collectives are active; migrate minimal KV pointer state so swapped kernels can resume without full recompile.
- Batching interaction: adjustments to scheduler to keep continuous batching work-stealing compatible with prefetcher decisions.
- Tests and perf harness: tests/tp/test_commcompute_conductor.py, bench/tp/bench_collectives.py and additions to perf-canary workflows.

Design notes and rationales: 
- Hierarchical scheduling groups GPUs into 'affinity shards' per-layer rather than forcing global synchronous collectives. This reduces head-of-line blocking for layers with small activations while preserving correctness for large-layer collectives. We calibrated window sizes with microbenchmarks on p4/p5 nodes.
- The prefetcher is intentionally conservative: it requires a prefix probability threshold before issuing Cross-node KV fetches; thresholds decay based on measured miss penalties to avoid flooding the network for bursty workloads.
- Kernel-swap provides low-cost fallbacks: we don't replace kernels wholesale, we annotate choices and perform fast pointer/mmap swaps; that keeps most of the runtime stable and minimizes JIT churn.

Commits in this PR (summary):
- commit 1: initial commcompute conductor state-machine and public hooks (author: Ethan Park)
- commit 2: KV prefetcher and metrics (histograms, per-peer counters, config knobs)
- commit 3: kernel swap paths and scheduler integration; tests + perf bench harness; docs update about rollout

Files changed (representative list):
- src/runtime/tp/commcompute_conductor.cc
- src/runtime/tp/commcompute_conductor.h
- src/runtime/nccl/pacing_policy.cc
- src/runtime/cache/kv_prefetcher.cc
- src/runtime/launcher/kernel_swap.cc
- src/runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching_integration.cc
- tests/tp/test_commcompute_conductor.py
- bench/tp/bench_collectives.py
- docs/notes/commcompute-conductor.md

Small illustrative diff (kernel annotation):
- @kernel(name="matmul_f16")
+ @kernel(name="matmul_f16", swap_hint="low_latency_fallback")

Benchmarks and results:
- Microbench on 8xA100-pod (tensor-parallel 4): end-to-end latency for 8-token generation workloads improved by 18% p50 and 24% p95 for typical prompt length (128 tokens) under continuous batching load.
- Allreduce overlap: measured 35% reduction in idle GPU cycles during large collective windows due to schedule interleaving.
- KV prefetch hit rate increased from 72% -> 88% for steady-state conversational traces in the internal perf corpus when prefetching enabled with threshold=0.6.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for conductor state transitions and prefetcher decay logic.
- Integration bench runs added to perf-canary pipeline to capture throughput/latency regressions.
- Initial CI flakiness: one GPU integration test failed on first run (OOM in python integration harness). Fixed by reducing temporary buffer sizes in kernel_swap and reran. Final CI status: all checks green.

Review conversation (high level, selected):
- Laura Mitchell (review): "Great high-level design. Please add explicit invariants for when prefetches are canceled (e.g. on model switch or prompt truncation). Also we should expose a runtime metric for speculative prefetch bandwidth."
  - Reply (Ethan): "Added prefetch cancellation hook and new metric prefetch_bytes_speculative. See kv_prefetcher.cc lines ~210-245."
- Ravi Kapoor (review): "Concern: kernel swap state migration could interact poorly with persistent caching; can we fail-safe to original kernel when migration fails?"
  - Reply (Ethan): "Yes — swap is guarded by atomic 'swap_ready' and we added fallback path to rebind original kernel; documented in comments and tests. Added unit to force swap failure to validate fallback."
- Anya Petrova (approval): "Bench look solid; happy to merge after CI is green and release notes."

Rollout plan:
- Canary: deploy conductor behind runtime flag on perf-canary and 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours. Monitor p50/p95 latencies, prefetch bytes, speculative miss rate, and GPU idle cycles.
- Gradual ramp: if canary metrics are stable (<2% reg on p50, improvement on tail), increase to 50% over 24h then full.
- Fallback: runtime flag disables all three components atomically if regression seen.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- No public API changes. Default prefetching is off for older models; conductor is controlled via runtime config flags. Kernel swap is opt-in via model-provided annotations.

Related work: links to ENG tickets and earlier PRs for NCCL pacing and KV-cache improvements (ENG-1345, ENG-1199). This PR integrates previously separate heuristics into a single conductor to reduce cross-component oscillation.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on: conductor state transitions (commcompute_conductor.h), prefetch threshold tuning code, and kernel swap fallback tests.
- Perf numbers included above were collected with the bench harness at bench/tp/bench_collectives.py; dataset used is internal-perf/conv-v2.

Merge outcome: PR was squashed and merged to main after CI passed and perf-canary smoke showed expected improvements.

Changelog (user-facing):
- Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel latency and throughput for many small-to-medium generation workloads via smarter overlap of collectives and compute, improved KV-cache prefetching, and low-cost kernel fallbacks.

If you want a walkthrough I can run a short demo showing conductor metrics in the console and the perf-canary dashboard.
